objective: Take up WEAK-APER-20261110-001's direction 1 (the same as RIGID-WORLDS-20261110-001#3 and BOARD-DIST-20261110-001#3) at the coordinator's go-ahead of 2026-11-10: challenge A54 by naming places without letters. Names are a countable set with no structure; each pair of names has a neighbour distinction and each name a value; laws are uniform over names. Ticket A proves what a law can then force: finitary laws always allow a structureless board (Ramsey); existence clauses supply a degree, and every board with even degree 2k carries k permutations, so the letters draw degree and connectivity and nothing more; count laws allow the universal cover of every board (the unfolding theorem without letters); no first-order law forces connected boards, and a named face with aperiodic tiles makes every component a plane; and boards are not frozen without letters, since edges with the same pair of values can exchange partners. Ticket B runs a frozen census of the 1,024 one-bit count laws: which knot the board with the values, and whether those knots are native.
stop_rule: One epic: targets T1 to T5 are each proved, refuted by a counterexample, or left with the gap stated; the census runs once on the frozen family, with no extension in this epic. Leibniz's rule with abstract names is out of scope. A54's status is then set by the frozen decision rule of the pre-registration.
title: Abstract names
